citation: Hellwig, Scarlata, Ackermann and Widmer, 'The Treebank of Vedic Sanskrit', LREC 2020; Hellwig, Nehrdich and Sellmer, 'Data-driven Dependency Parsing of Vedic Sanskrit', LRE 57:1173-1206, 2023.
reference_scope_limit: It annotates the Vedic text. It does not annotate VedaGraph's claims, so it can decide whether a word is in a verse and which word it is, and it cannot decide whether a verse is *about* a concept.
title: UD_Sanskrit-Vedic (the Treebank of Vedic Sanskrit)
what_it_covers: 27,182 sentences / 206,440 words over 57 Vedic texts. In scope for this corpus: RV 4,352 sentences, AVS 2,175, VSM 622. The Samaveda is absent, which is the third independent negative on Samavedic morphology after DCS and VedaWeb.

title: VedaWeb / Zurich Rigveda lemmatisation, as already cited in the graph
used_for: the deity-to-lemma bridge, and as the second independent witness that a treebank sentence was addressed to the right verse.
what_it_covers: Per-token lemma and morphology for the Rigveda. Not fetched: it is read out of the graph's own MENTIONS_DEVATA evidence quotes, which carry the Zurich lemma and case verbatim, and out of the 10,031 :Lemma nodes.

title: The canonical VedaGraph Neo4j store, read-only
